# Hanshin Takes Control Early and Beats Hiroshima 8-1

On August 16, 2026, the Hanshin Tigers beat the Hiroshima Toyo Carp 8-1 at MAZDA Zoom-Zoom Stadium Hiroshima.

The story of the game was simple: Hanshin moved first, and then kept control.

Hanshin took a 2-0 lead with a two-run home run in the first inning. That gave the team an early advantage and put pressure on Hiroshima from the start.

Takato Ihara then gave that lead a strong base. The Hanshin starter worked five innings, allowed only two hits, and gave up one run.

Hiroshima’s only run came in the fifth inning. Elehuris Montero hit a solo home run. The score became 2-1, but Hiroshima could not add another run.

Hanshin added more runs in the seventh and eighth innings. Seishiro Sakamoto and Torai Fushimi delivered important hits, and Sakamoto added another run with a double.

The lead grew, and Hiroshima had no answer late in the game.

The final score was:

Hanshin Tigers 8, Hiroshima Toyo Carp 1.

This was not a close escape. It was a win built in steps: an early strike, steady pitching, and more runs near the end.

### Sato’s big swing had a deeper story

With two outs and a runner on first, Teruaki Sato faced Shohei Mori. The count was one ball and one strike. Sato hit Mori’s third pitch, a two-seam fastball, for his 28th home run. He moved to within one home run of teammate Shota Morishita. One swing won that moment and brought Sato closer in the team’s home-run race.

### A win that stopped two slides

This victory also changed the short-term picture. It stopped Hanshin’s two-game losing streak and kept the Tigers in first place, two games ahead of the Giants. Hiroshima’s own two-game winning streak ended before it could become three. So the result held Hanshin’s position and stopped Hiroshima from building more momentum.

## In one line…

A quick home run gave Hanshin the lead, but Ihara’s steady work and late runs turned that start into a complete 8-1 victory.
